question: Which of the following molecules participates in the extravasation of the T lymphocytes to the target tissue ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Selectina L" -> "binds to endothelial cells" -> "facilitates rolling of T lymphocytes" -> "extravasation to target tissue" -> 95%
CHAIN: "IFN-gamma" -> "activates macrophages" -> "enhances immune response" -> "possible indirect effect on extravasation" -> 50%
CHAIN: "CD3" -> "part of T cell receptor complex" -> "signal transduction in T cells" -> "not directly involved in extravasation" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Molecules belonging to the MHC" -> "present antigens to T cells" -> "involved in immune recognition" -> "not directly involved in extravasation" -> 40%
analysis: Extravasation of T lymphocytes involves their movement from the bloodstream into tissues, a process that requires adhesion molecules. Selectins, including Selectin L (L-selectin), play a crucial role in the initial step of this process by mediating the rolling of lymphocytes along the vascular endothelium. This is followed by firm adhesion and transmigration into the tissue. Therefore, Selectin L is directly involved in the extravasation of T lymphocytes.
